WHY IT IS FATAL TO THE UNIFORM READING, which is thread 66's own statement of the problem: the 2026-10-11 batch's maximum-lookbehind row returned the sort strip verbatim - 'Pending Cases Concluded Cases Recent Cases Recent Cases Registered Published Concluded Constituted October 6, 2026 Lombard ...' - FOUR date-type labels, NO case-name header, each entry's date rendering BEFORE its name. On that reading 'September 16, 2026' binds to ARB/18/20, and an ARB/18/xx designator is not a 2026 registration. So either the page is a union of four recency feeds in which each entry carries the date of the event that put it there, or the date-before-name binding is wrong. UNTIL IT IS SETTLED, NO DATE ON /cases/recent MAY BE READ AS A REGISTRATION DATE - that prohibition is in force now and this batch does not lift it; only a reading of these rows can. PRIOR ART ON THIS EXACT URL, SCREENED BEFORE WRITING (prior-art screen on instrument claims, thread 51): this page has been fetched ONCE, on 2026-09-18 (2026-09-18-daily.json idx 7), find 'Subject of Dispute', find_matched TRUE, ok/200/text-html, 103,808 bytes, returning ICSID's own labelled triple verbatim: 'Subject of Dispute: Renewable energy generation enterprise Economic Sector: Electric Power & Other Energy Instrument(s) Invoked: (i) ECT (Energy Charter Treaty) Applicable Rules: ICSID Convention'. (i) THE UNENCODED URL FORM 'CaseNo=ARB/18/20' IS CERTIFIED 200 ON THIS HOST by that row, so every row below uses it; the percent-encoded form has never been fired on this matter and is not used here. (ii) THE MATTER IS AN ECT RENEWABLE-ENERGY MATTER WITH NO IP, PHARMACEUTICAL, TRADE-SECRET OR CLINICAL-DATA NEXUS WHATEVER. THIS BATCH IS THEREFORE NOT RESEARCH INTO THE RESEARCH QUESTION AND MAY NEVER BE WRITTEN UP AS SUCH. No seat may convert any row below into a finding about intellectual property as a covered investment, about any ring, or about Italy, Veolia or the Energy Charter Treaty. SO ROW 2 IS A FIRST FIRING OF A LITERAL WITH ONE PRIOR FALSE ON ANOTHER PAGE FAMILY, and a FALSE on row 2 is an INSTRUMENT OBSERVATION about label rendering on this page, NEVER a statement that the matter has no registration date. NOTE ON MULTIPLE OCCURRENCES, binding on how row 2 is read: excerpt_of searches with body.lower().find() (scripts/fetch_relay.py:131), which returns the FIRST occurrence only. 'Date Registered' occurs more than once on pages carrying annulment or revision proceedings - ARB/12/1 renders it at January 12, 2012 for the original proceeding and again at November 18, 2019 for the annulment and March 16, 2021 for the revision. Row 2 therefore returns the FIRST such label in document order and nothing about any later one. If the window's date is a 2018 date the original-proceeding reading is corroborated by document order; if it is not, NO INFERENCE is available about which proceeding it belongs to without a further row, and none may be drawn. WHAT EACH OUTCOME WOULD AND WOULD NOT SETTLE, FIXED HERE BEFORE THE ROWS FIRE. (A) If row 2 returns a 2018 registration date AND row 3 ('September 16, 2026') returns TRUE with that date adjacent to a labelled event on this page, then the date-before-name binding on /cases/recent HOLDS and the page is confirmed a union of feeds in which the date is the date of whichever feed event listed the entry - and the standing prohibition hardens into a permanent rule rather than lifting, because the row itself still does not say WHICH feed listed any given entry. (B) If row 2 returns a 2018 date and row 3 returns FALSE while row 4 hits, then 'September 16, 2026' is absent from this matter's own 100-kilobyte page while being rendered next to its name on /cases/recent, and the date-before-name binding is IMPEACHED - which kills the technique, exactly as thread 66 says it might. (C) If rows 1-4 all miss, the batch is UNINTERPRETABLE as to this page and goes back as an instrument observation. NO OTHER READING IS AUTHORISED, and in particular no row below founds a count, a rate, an ordinal fact, or any statement about how ICSID populates any feed.
